sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with strong commercial law codification (Código de Comercio) and common law influences in corporate and trust practices
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) implemented through Ley 10 of 2012
Agreement on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (BIT) with the United Kingdom (in force 1985)
Panama–European Union Association Agreement (political dialogue and cooperation, trade pillar in negotiation status)
Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs) with Netherlands, Mexico, Singapore, Luxembourg, Korea, Portugal, Qatar, Barbados, UAE, Curaçao, Spain, France, Italy, and others

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (as amended by Law 202 of 2021) on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism; Cabinet Decree No. 1 of 2021 (SBR Supervision); Resolution No. 003-2022 of the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF); Unique Beneficiary Register (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) created by Law 52 of 27 October 2016 and regulated by Executive Decree No. 406 of 2019, with amendments under Law 70 of 2021; General Resolutions of the Superintendency of Banks regulating AML/CFT for obliged non-regulated entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Legal Capacity (Certificado de Persona Jurídica / Derecho Legal) for the shareholder entity or personal identification document (cédula / passport) of beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry) for corporate shareholders; Notario Público (Notary) for certified copies of personal identification or corporate documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a Contracting State to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961, effective 4 February 2008); documents issued outside Panama must be apostilled by the competent authority of the origin country; documents in non-Spanish language must be translated into Spanish by an authorized translator and legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, Register of Directors, or Power of Attorney granted to the incorporation agent (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal or trust company in the jurisdiction where the beneficial owner is a corporate entity; notarized in the origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or negative PEP (Politically Exposed Person) declaration and source of funds affidavit for each individual beneficial owner holding at least 10% equity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or independent external auditor in the applicant’s country of residence; the declaration is signed before a Notary Public in Panama or abroad (apostilled if abroad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries; Hague Apostille for member states; otherwise Panamanian Consular attestation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all natural person beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, FATF Mutual Evaluation List, and Panamanian National Sanctions List maintained by the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero). Enhanced due diligence is required when a beneficial owner or senior officer is designated as a PEP, including verification of source of wealth and continuous transaction monitoring. Negative news and adverse media checks offset via reliable databases are compulsory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Personas Jurídicas Online Platform (acquire via authorized notary or law firm using the S.E.C. (Sistema de Entradas y Certificaciones) portal or the Notary’s Direct Access system; public name search available through www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Spanish, English, or another language using Latin alphabet characters. If in a non-Latin script, a transliteration to Latin characters is required, and the company name must be capable of being reproduced in Spanish for registration. Use of Latin characters only; diacritics and special symbols are restricted. The presence of the words 'Sociedad Anónima' or its acceptable abbreviation 'S.A.' must either form part of the proposed name or be included as a separate mandatory appendix; the Registry’s approval is issued for a single exclusive name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Compañía de Seguros, Reaseguradora, Financiera (Financial institution terms requiring SBP authorization)
Fondo de Inversión (requires CNV/Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores license)
Seguro(s), Fianza, Reaseguro (Insurance terms requiring Superintendencia de Seguros approval)
Trust, Fideicomiso, Fundación privada de interés privado (Foundation/trust regulatory approval needed)
Abogado, Notario, Auditor, Contador, Consultor Legal (professional services restrictions)
Canal (Canal-related terms reserved for Panama Canal Authority / ACP)
Caja de Ahorros and other government institution names protected by national law
Juegos, Casino, Apuestas (gambling terms requiring Comisión de Juegos license)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (General Law of Sociedades Anónimas of Panama), as amended, Articles 1-7 (formation and deed content), Article 19 (registered shares), Article 26 (resident agent); supplementary provisions of the Código de Comercio (Articles 1375 et seq.) and Ley 5 de 2015 (registered share regime and abolition of bearer shares).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General, Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Section of the Public Registry of Panama), Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Incorporation Deed) executed before a Notary Public of the Republic of Panama and inscribed in the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under Ley 32 de 1927. The Escritura Pública must state the authorized capital, commonly USD 10,000 divided into registered common shares; the capital may be fully subscribed with deferred payment and no escrow, deposit or banked capital account is mandated. Additional registry inscription fees apply if the authorized capital exceeds USD 10,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The subscriptions to the capital stock of the Company are ratified and accepted, and the capital is declared fully subscribed. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address], Republic of Panama, and the appointment of [Firm], lawyer, as Resident Agent is ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER: The persons named below are elected as officers: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary; [Name], Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting and to act individually in ordinary management. RESOLVED FURTHER: The form of share certificate is adopted, the corporate books are opened, and the officers are authorized to execute the Escritura Pública and all ancillary registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Verification and Drafting of the Escritura Pública
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección de Información (online name search portal) and a Notary Public of the First Judicial Circuit, Panama City.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-search request through the Registro Público online platform or in person to verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. Upon clearance, instruct the drafting attorney to prepare the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the mandatory clauses: corporate name, corporate object limited to ISIC 6201 software services and no-code website builder activities, authorized capital, registered share classes, resident agent appointment and initial officer structure.
required_dossiers: Passport or identity document of each subscriber/shareholder
Draft articles of incorporation and by-laws
Notarized power of attorney if a subscriber acts through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or formally queried, file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) with the Registro Público within the applicable legal period, or amend the draft deed to use an approved alternative name before notarization; no re-notarization cost arises if the deed has not yet been executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Public Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Notary Public of the First Judicial Circuit, Panama City).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers or their duly authorized attorneys-in-fact must appear personally before the notary to sign the Escritura Pública de Constitución. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, records the declarations required under Ley 32 de 1927, protocols the deed, and issues the testimonio (certified first copy). Municipal fiscal stamps (papel sellado) and notarial fees are settled at the time of execution.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the incorporation deed
Valid passport or national ID of each subscriber
Proof of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects deficiencies in identity documents or signature discrepancies, an order of correction (orden de subsanación) is issued; formal errors are cured by a marginal note while substantive defects require a rectifying instrument (nueva escritura) executed before the same notary and re-protocolized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Public Registry Inscription Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá and Registro Público de Panamá - Caja (Collection Window), Panama City.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the statutory registry inscription fee (approximately USD 135.00 for the first five folios plus additional per-folio charges) using the official fee planilla. Deposit the amount at the Banco Nacional de Panamá or the Registro Público collection window and obtain the stamped payment receipt. Attach the receipt to the deed file as mandatory proof of payment before inscription.
required_dossiers: Notarized testimonio of the Escritura Pública
Fee computation sheet (planilla de derecho de inscripción)
Payment receipt issued by Banco Nacional de Panamá or the Registry cashier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry recalculates the fee or detects underpayment, pay the differential amount plus any applicable surcharge at the Caja and obtain an amended receipt; the registry appends a payment note (nota de pago) to the deed record prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Inscription of the Corporation at the Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Section).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first-copy testimonio of the Escritura Pública together with the fee receipt at the Mercantile Section registry window or through the authorized online filing module. The registry examiner (revisor) reviews the deed for formal and legal compliance; upon approval, the inscription is effected and the Sociedad Anónima acquires legal personality as of the date of inscription. The registry issues a certificate of entry evidencing the incorporation.
required_dossiers: First-copy testimonio of the Escritura Pública
Notarized power of attorney of the applying attorney (if applicable)
Signed application for inscription (solicitud de inscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the revisor issues a defect report (observación) or correction notice, the applicant must submit a correction petition (escritura de enmienda or salvedad) within 30 days addressing each observation; purely formal defects may be cured by a marginal note authorized by the Head of the Mercantile Section, subject to a reduced re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening and Legalization of Corporate Books and Registered Office Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Legalización de Libros; Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipalidad de Panamá for ancillary post-formation filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, open the statutory corporate records: Libro de Acciones (share register), Libro de Actas (minutes book) and Libro de Dividendos as applicable. Present the blank hardbound books to the Registro Público for legalization within the statutory period. Finalize the registered office arrangement with the Resident Agent, obtain the RUC tax identification number from DGI, and note the obligation to file the annual franchise tax notice before 31 March of the following year.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscription entry (copia certificada de la inscripción)
Registered office lease agreement or Resident Agent acceptance letter
DGI taxpayer registration form (RUC) - post-formation filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate books are presented late for legalization, pay the statutory late fee (multa) imposed by the Registro Público and proceed with legalization immediately after payment; the registry issues a certification of legality confirming compliance for subsequent banking or contracting purposes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección General de Actividades Comerciales; however, no industrial operating or manufacturing license is mandated for the ISIC 6201 no-code website builder activity, which is a service-type operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable as an industrial license. Only the municipal Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Notice) issued by the Alcaldía de Panamá is required when the company maintains physical premises or hires local employees; no manufacturing permit applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Registro / Evaluación Ambiental Simplificada) or exempt: office-based software development and no-code platform services generate no significant environmental impact; a full Estudio de Impacto Ambiental (EIA) is not required for a standard Class I office use, unless construction works or facilities exceeding the regulatory floor-area thresholds are involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or particulate emissions are generated by the core activity; office sanitary effluents must comply with IDAAN municipal sewer standards, solid waste must be separated under municipal ordinance and collected by authorized operators, and any standby electrical generator must meet MiAMBIENTE air quality emission limits under Decreto Ejecutivo 43 de 2015.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios) required from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for any physical office premises; structural pre-occupancy load inspection by the Dirección de Obras y Construcciones of the Municipalidad de Panamá; occupational health, electrical safety and workplace ergonomics compliance under MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral) and Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) regulations once employees are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Official portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa; taxpayer e-services, RUC administration, tax filing and e-invoicing are accessed through the DGI e-Tax/SICAI portal and the separate Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (FEP).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Sociedad Anónima at the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed attorney; a resident agent is mandatory. 2) File the municipal Aviso de Operación with the competent municipality, or use the Ventanilla Única de Registro de Empresas (VURE). 3) Apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) online at DGI e-Tax using Form Solicitud de RUC, attaching the Escritura Pública, Registro Público certificate, legal representative identification, municipal Aviso de Operación, and sworn statement of fiscal domicile; the ITBMS registration is activated on the same RUC by electing the Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios obligation. 4) Activate the electronic invoicing profile in the FEP portal and obtain the digital stamp certificate. 5) A non-resident foreign digital service provider without a Panamanian establishment must register under the simplified Proveedores de Servicios Digitales regime through a tax representative, obtaining a NIT/RUC for ITBMS collection and reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (territorial scope: Panama-source income only; a Panamanian S.A. is a separate juridical person subject to corporate income tax at the entity level, but foreign-source income remains outside the Panamanian tax base. Pass-through treatment is not available.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election; classification as a taxable S.A. is per se. Available statutory elections and special regimes include: fiscal group consolidation for corporate income tax; simplified registration and remittance regime for foreign digital service suppliers; advance pricing agreements for related-party cross-border service transactions; election of monthly advance payments with annual final ISR settlement; small-taxpayer ITBMS threshold regime for local micro operations; and the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime under Ley 41 de 2007 where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panama's VAT/GST system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 300,000 of annual gross taxable turnover for domestic taxable persons (registration required once the threshold is exceeded); foreign non-established digital service providers must register and remit ITBMS when their annual supplies of digital/e-services to Panama exceed USD 150,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory phased electronic invoicing under the Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (FEP) regime. All registered taxpayers must issue electronic invoices in XML/JSON to the DGI fiscal clearance platform. Online mode requires real-time submission to DGI and receipt of an electronic Autorización before the invoice is delivered to the customer, with API integration for software vendors. Offline mode requires a cryptographic Sello Digital and transmission of the signed XML file to DGI within the prescribed batch window, with QR-code validation. Foreign digital service providers may use the simplified e-receipt module of the FEP portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS export zero-rating is available where: (i) the recipient of the service is domiciled or established outside Panama; (ii) the no-code website builder service, visual templates and SaaS platform are delivered remotely and effectively used, enjoyed or economically exploited entirely outside Panama; (iii) payment originates from abroad and is received into a Panamanian bank account; and (iv) the Panamanian exporter holds a valid RUC/ITBMS registration and files the sworn Certificado de Exportación de Servicios / export declaration with the DGI. Sales to Panamanian customers or any local use of the software trigger the standard 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera / DUA) for physical goods; not required for pure digital no-code software services
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or original bank statement showing receipt of export proceeds from abroad through the Panamanian banking system
Certificado de Exportación de Servicios or sworn declaration filed with the DGI
Commercial invoice and signed service agreement identifying the foreign customer and the offshore use/benefit of the software
User-activity logs, IP-based customer localization report or server-access evidence demonstrating that the service is consumed outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a high-risk DGI audit area. If the substantiation file is incomplete or the foreign-remittance evidence is inconsistent, the DGI may retroactively reverse the 0% rate and assess the standard 7% ITBMS on the gross invoice amount, plus statutory late-payment interest. Where fraud, forgery or fictitious exports are detected, the law authorizes fines of 100%-300% of the omitted tax, clawback of any refunded ITBMS with interest, and criminal tax fraud prosecution under Panama's delitos tributarios framework with imprisonment of up to 8 years. Directors and the legal representative may be held personally liable in cases of gross fraud. The DGI may reassess within the general five-year limitation period, which is extended where concealment or fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no independent central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) regulates the banking sector, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent for the government. The U.S. dollar is legal tender, and Panama does not issue its own currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian economy is fully dollarized; capital and current account transactions are freely convertible with zero exchange-control restrictions. There are no restrictions on inflow or outflow of foreign currency, no differential exchange rates, and no foreign-exchange licensing or approval requirements. Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriation may be executed freely without government authorization, subject to standard bank compliance and corporate tax filings. Withholding tax obligations apply only if the distribution is solvent and properly documented.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama does not operate an export-proceeds surrender regime. There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio requiring exporters to sell or deposit foreign currency with any domestic bank. Receipts may be retained in any denomination, held offshore, or settled through any freely chosen correspondent bank. Financial institutions may still require documentary evidence of the underlying export transaction for AML/KYC purposes, typically a commercial invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration, but they do not enforce any FX surrender obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Multi-currency Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC Credomatic Panama (BAC International Bank Group)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Local Institutional Operating Account / Government-linked Escrow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Panama does not have a passportable EU-style EMI licence. Offshore digital EMIs and payment service providers can be used only as supplementary treasury rails, not as primary bank accounts, because they generally do not provide insured deposit custody, IBAN access, or full credit intermediation. Panama’s SBP regulates payment and settlement services under a 'Try-and-Adapt' fintech sandbox; a locally registered investment company or a Payment Service Provider licence (subject to SBP approval) is required for a regulated in-country fintech presence. For cross-border SaaS treasury, using a reputable U.S./EU EMI for operational collections is viable but must be layered with an SBP-regulated Panama bank for peak cash concentration, capital escrow, and corporate investor wire settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners of a Sociedad Anónima are generally required to appear physically or be identified via secure videoconferencing with a Panama-licensed lawyer or notary. Most tier-1 banks require at least one senior officer (President, Treasurer, or CFO) to appear in person at the branch for the initial onboarding interview, especially when the entity is non-resident-owned. Remote opening is increasingly possible, but only where (a) all shareholders, directors, and UBOs obtain notarized and apostilled identification documents from their country of residence; (b) a Panamanian legal counsel orescrow agent acts as introducer; and (c) the bank obtains a certified copy of the public deed of incorporation, corporate bylaws (pacto social), registry certificate (personería jurídica), and a full corporate/UBO information sheet. Physical presence is strongly recommended for the first signatory; subsequent new signatories may be added through written armed-insignature exports, subject to bank policy. Remote-only onboardings often have longer approval cycles and may be flagged for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership / offshore legal form (Sociedad Anónima domiciled in Panama but controlled by foreign natural persons)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full notarized and apostilled corporate registry record (Ficha Registral), certified copy of the public deed, current Personería Jurídica, updated UBO declaration with passport copies and original utility/bank statements, plus a signed sworn affidavit explaining the source of wealth and source of funds. Include a current Panama legal opinion letter confirming that the entity is not an 'offshore shell' but holds a genuine business operation (e.g., website template subscription platform) with identifiable employees and customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound capital from crypto-adjacent or high-volume low-ticket payment rails (Stripe, Paddle)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a full treasury model showing expected monthly revenue, customer invoice exports, billing-platform settlements, and reconciliation statements. Provide independent traceability: Stripe/Paddle legal terms, tax-exemption certificate (or tax registration) if applicable, and a company bank-reference letter from the originating bank where the payment-rail settlement account is held. If any nuance of crypto or stablecoin settlement is reportedly involved, include a legal memo proving that all inbound settlement funds are fiat-denominated and that no unlicensed crypto exchange is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Minimum capital has not been contributed (Panama does not require paid-in capital for S.A., but banks may reject zero-capital structures)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute a board-resolution authorizing a capital contribution (even if minimal, e.g., USD 10,000) and deposit it into a temporary internal account; present the notarized equity-transfer statement, the bank receipt proving capital custodia, and a post-contribution certified capital statement. Alternatively, show that the juridical person is receiving paid-in capital from verified shareholders via SWIFT MT103 with explicit purpose code 'Investment in shares (Código 1000)' or 'Capital contribution', with supporting shareholder agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: U.S.-based ultimate shareholder or founder with Panama corporate only (potential 'US person in Panama entity' red flag due to FATCA)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain a Panama legal/audit opinion confirming that the Panamanian entity has no U.S. sourced income and is not a 'passive foreign investment company' under U.S. rules. Submit IRS Form W-8BEN-E so the bank can evidence beneficial owner's non-U.S. status. For U.S. citizens, provide a W-9 and explain the tax compliance status via an international tax attorney letter; the bank will open the account only after FATCA clearance and will include the CRS/FATCA legal-form package.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical office / shared virtual address in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed lease or official corporate registered-agent receipt (of the law firm acting as resident agent), current municipal license (Aviso de Operación) if the company has any local activity, and an on-the-ground compliance officer (the local legal counsel) who can represent the entity during bank site visits. If no physical office exists, use a 'virtual office' arrangement with a reputable third-party provider, and attach the service agreement and corporate resolution authorizing the use of a virtual office address for official correspondence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders must be executed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for high-value interbank settlement) through a reputable correspondent bank. The 'purpose of payment' must unambiguously state the nature of the funds: for equity subscription use 'Contribution of capital (Aporte de Capital)' or SWIFT field 72/77B note 'CAPITAL INJECTION'; for shareholder loans use 'Loan – intercompany financing' and reference a signed loan agreement. Panama has no exchange-control approval, but the receiving bank will require around USD 10,000+ to evidence source of funds: notarized/shareholder board resolution approving the capital increase, wire instruction from the shareholder’s owned account (not third-party), a corporate certificate listing shares issued, and a record of the internal capital movement (Asset and Liability register). Banks apply a 0.25%–0.50% commission for high-value inbound wires, and funds are typically available within 1–2 banking days. Wire transfers from offshore jurisdictions or fintech wallets may be blocked unless an 'Economic Substance Equivalent' note is attached; therefore, route all investments directly from the investor's bank account in the same legal name as the shareholder in the corporate documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade and operational disbursements, Panama’s clearing rails are fully USD-based. Settlement is achieved via (a) domestic ACH/RTGS clearing within Panama's Cámara de Compensación Interbancaria (for local vendor invoices); (b) correspondent U.S. Dollar clearing via Fedwire or CHIPS for payments into the United States; (c) SWIFT MT103 for international transfers outside Panama; and (d) Commercial Letters of Credit issued through a Panamanian commercial bank under UCP600 for international best-way trade transactions. For software vendor payments and API platform obligations (e.g., Stripe, AWS), the issuer must pre-clear the vendor name on the bank's OFAC/fintech integration list; payment instructions should include a granular invoice reference, (preferably) remittance via a 'Expected Credit Application' (CTA), and a unique transaction ID (UTI). Bank settlement times for MT103 outside Panama are typically T+1 or T+2. For large cross-border disbursements exceeding USD 100,000, banks may impose an FX rate margin (if not in USD) and require an underlying contract or invoice for FX administrative purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards (short-dated USD/foreign currency forwards) executed with an SBP-regulated bank or international counterparty, where the corporate has a documented foreign-exchange exposure (e.g., EUR, GBP, CAD).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are rare but permissible where the currency of the operational currency (e.g., Argentine Peso, local-currency receivables) is not fully market-convertible; settlement in USD only, but Panama does not impose restrictions on buying hedging products from international banks.

Cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-fixed USD/EUR or USD/GBP) available from top-tier global corporate banks with a Panama domicile, but the entity must demonstrate a treasury purpose, not speculative intent.

Plain-vanilla FX option structures (call/put on EUR, GBP) with international investment banks, allowable for netting and risk management; no Panamanian exchange approval is required. Note: given that Panama is fully dollarized, and for a low-risk SaaS build, the simplest and most compliant hedge is to keep invoices in USD and only execute short-date forward trades via the clearing bank's treasury desk when a material contractual exposure arises in non-USD currency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tasa Única – annual Panamanian corporate franchise tax for the Sociedad Anónima
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually between 1 January and 31 March to apply the base rate of USD 300; the fee escalates to USD 350 if paid by 30 June, USD 400 by 30 September, and USD 500 by 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Progressive late-payment escalator up to USD 500; statutory interest on overdue amounts; DGI and Registro Público will not issue Paz y Salvo (good standing certificate); Registro Público refuses registration of corporate documents; persistent delinquency risks administrative suspension of the corporate registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta) for the S.A.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 March for the calendar year ended 31 December; the deadline is extended to 15 April for online filing and payment through the DGI e-portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10% of the tax due for the first month of delay and an additional 10% for each subsequent month or fraction, capped at 50%; statutory interest on unpaid tax; minimum fine of USD 100 for failure to file, with higher fines for repeat non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (Estados Financieros, audited or unaudited)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – electronic submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual income tax return: 31 March, extended to 15 April for online filers; audited statements are compulsory when annual gross income exceeds USD 500,000 or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same surcharge and interest regime as the annual return; incomplete or rejected financial statements trigger separate fines of USD 100 to USD 1,000 and may cause disallowance of deductions claimed in the return

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party transaction information report (Informe de Operaciones con Terceros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, extended to 15 April for online filers, covering the preceding calendar year; applicable when aggregate third-party transactions, including Stripe and Paddle settlements, exceed USD 20,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 100 to USD 500 for each unfiled or incomplete report; unresolved delinquency blocks DGI enrollment updates and may reopen prior tax years for assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Aviso de Operación – annual business operation notice renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alcaldía (Municipality) of the registered office, typically Distrito de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter, due by 31 March for the Municipality of Panama; base fixed fee of approximately USD 100 to USD 250 plus a municipal gross-receipts tax of 1% to 2% on locally sourced revenues
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal surcharges and interest; suspension of the Aviso de Operación; fines up to USD 1,000; referral to the Registro Público as a non-operating entity, which can impair future corporate filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO registry annual confirmation and change-of-ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial UBO declaration within 30 days of incorporation; updated declaration within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation aligned with the Tasa Única payment cycle, due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 1,000 to USD 5,000 for untimely or incomplete filings; knowingly false UBO information subject to penalties up to USD 50,000; delinquency blocks all Registro Público and DGI transactions for the corporation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a Panamanian S.A. when annual gross income exceeds USD 500,000 (B/. 500,000) or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000 (B/. 3,000,000); the audit must be performed by a Panamanian Contador Público Autorizado and the audited financial statements must be filed electronically with the DGI together with the annual income tax return; entities below the thresholds may file unaudited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Panama; small and medium-sized entities may apply IFRS for SMEs; there is no separate local GAAP, and the Balboa is at par with the U.S. dollar, so statutory reporting currency is USD.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2020, the S.A. must file initial beneficial-ownership data with the DGI RUBF registry within 30 days of incorporation and must update the registry within 30 days of any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial owner. The annual confirmation is collected together with the Tasa Única payment: the resident agent certifies that beneficial owners and percentage holdings are unchanged, and any modification is declared through the DGI e-portal. A UBO filing is a precondition for obtaining a certificate of good standing from the Registro Público, and a non-compliant corporation cannot lawfully execute certain corporate acts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registro de Accionistas), including details of any immobilised bearer-share positions
Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas)
Board of Directors' Meeting Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva)
Share Transfer Ledger (Libro de Transferencia de Acciones)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 900 per year for a Panama City licensed resident agent and registered office package, excluding government fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 for a certified audit of a low-volume SaaS holding entity; unaudited compilation or review engagements typically range from USD 800 to USD 1,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is subject to corporate income tax, while foreign-source income of an ordinary Panamanian Sociedad Anónima is outside the taxable base. There is no general statutory tax holiday for an ordinary unlicensed S.A., but specialized regimes (Multinational Headquarters or SEM, Panama Pacifico, City of Knowledge, and export processing zones) can reduce effective tax rates for qualified license-holders. The ordinary S.A. may reduce Panama-source taxable income with directly attributable operating deductions; expenses allocated to exempt foreign-source income must be excluded. Tax loss carryforward is available for five fiscal years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: DGI Renta e-Return — Declaración Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta (Corporate Module) filed through the official electronic portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI en Línea / e-Tax 2.0)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 December fiscal year, the annual corporate income tax return is due on or before 15 March of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the return is due no later than the fifteenth day of the third month after the fiscal year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from commercial, industrial and service activities carried out or realized in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only Panama-source revenue. For a no-code SaaS builder, exclude subscription revenue allocated to foreign users where the service is sourced as foreign income and is not effectively linked to a Panama place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income and income exempt from tax by law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a foreign-source revenue schedule showing the territorial sourcing analysis, customer location, execution location, and server or IP-licensing arrangements. The burden of proving foreign-source treatment lies with the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to Panama-source income, including software development, hosting, marketing, salaries, rent, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for intercompany costs. If all revenue is foreign-source, expenses attributable to that foreign-source income must be isolated and cannot reduce Panama taxable income unless the DGI recharacterizes the substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: Panama-source gross revenue minus deductible expenses, adjusted for statutory disallowances and add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company has no Panama-source revenue and no Panama office, net taxable income may be zero, but the annual return and the corporate registry annual fee must still be filed and paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 25% on net taxable income before credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not use foreign income tax credits against Panama corporate tax unless specifically covered by a Panama tax treaty or domestic law; Panama generally taxes on a territorial basis and does not grant ordinary foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, withholding credits, and tax prepayments applied against the annual corporate income tax charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all payments made to the DGI. Non-resident owners should not take distributions or management fees unless dividend withholding and substance considerations are addressed in the annual file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return incurs a surcharge of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of a month of delay, up to a maximum of 50% of the tax due. Late payment accrues monthly default interest, generally at approximately 1% per month. Where no tax is due, the DGI may impose fixed administrative fines for delinquency. Continuing noncompliance blocks good-standing certificates and can result in collection measures, asset attachment, and registry strike-off for the S.A.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends paid by a Panamanian S.A. out of Panama taxable income. Where dividends are paid from exempt foreign-source retained earnings, the territorial characterization must be fully documented to avoid DGI reclassification; if the source analysis fails, the 10% withholding may be asserted on the gross distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder seeking treaty relief must obtain a tax residency certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from its home tax authority, submit the certificate together with a beneficial ownership declaration and the applicable DGI treaty-relief form to the Panamanian paying company, and retain copies in the accounting records for DGI inspection. The payer reports the reduced withholding rate on the dividend withholding return and must be able to present the treaty analysis. Panama DTAs generally reduce dividend withholding to 5% or 15% depending on shareholding level and the particular treaty; where no DTA exists, the statutory 10% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama-source royalty payments to a non-resident for the use of software IP, trademarks, know-how and similar intangibles are generally subject to statutory withholding of 12.5% of the gross remittance, derived from the deemed 50% net-base rule applied at the 25% CIT rate. Interest paid to a non-resident lender on financing used in Panama is also generally subject to 12.5% statutory withholding; offshore syndicated loans, documented foreign financing, and certain approved international business activities may qualify for exemption or reduced rates. Under most Panama DTAs, the withholding on royalties and interest can be reduced to between 0% and 10%, subject to submission of a valid residency certificate and beneficial ownership confirmation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama applies arm's length transfer pricing rules to related-party transactions. Mandatory documentation, including Local File and Master File requirements, is triggered where aggregate related-party transactions equal or exceed PAB 1,000,000 (USD 1,000,000) in a fiscal year, or where gross revenue exceeds PAB 2,000,000 (USD 2,000,000) and related-party transactions are material. The DGI may request a transfer pricing study in any audit, regardless of threshold, where connected software development fees, IP royalties, or intercompany management charges are present.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations, principally Law 254 of 2021, require Panamanian legal entities to demonstrate real economic presence when undertaking relevant activities or claiming zero or foreign-source tax treatment. A no-code website builder must show that its Panamanian office, employees, board decisions, and operational control are proportionate to the revenue held in the company. The absence of local offices, local staff, or real business control while foreign-source income is booked through Panama will allow the DGI to classify the S.A. as a shell and recharacterize the income as Panama-source, with treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly classifying Panama-source subscription revenues as foreign-source, failing to file the annual CIT return, submitting false revenue schedules, or using artificial invoices to strip profits out of the Panamanian S.A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of the underpaid 25% corporate income tax, plus monthly interest and late-filing surcharges of up to 50% of the tax due. Criminal tax fraud can result in fines of multiple times the evaded tax and imprisonment for the individuals who sign or direct the false return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false declarations can be personally and jointly liable for the tax deficiency through piercing of the corporate veil; civil restitution, asset freezes, passport retention, travel bans, and imprisonment up to five years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a foreign affiliate above-market fees for software developers, charging excessive royalties for low-code platform IP, or recording large intercompany management fees as disguised profit repatriation without arm's length support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjustment of income to the arm's length standard, reversal of excessive deductions, assessment of back tax with monthly interest, penalties ranging from 10% to 40% of the adjusted tax amount, and fixed fines for failure to file transfer pricing informative returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving nonsensical transfer prices without documentation may be jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties. In a fiscal audit, travel bans and seizure of personal assets can be ordered when willful misconduct is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panama S.A. with no office, no employees, no bank-controlled substance, and no local decision-making to hold SaaS IP and worldwide subscription revenue while claiming zero Panama taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the shell company as a Panama tax-resident and taxable enterprise, reclassification of revenue as Panama-source, denial of treaty benefits, economic substance fines under Law 254 of 2021, and cancellation of the corporate registration where false declarations are found.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in a sham substance structure may be investigated under Panama anti-money laundering law (Ley 23 de 2015); they face civil restitution, confiscation of property, travel bans, director disqualification, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders without applying the statutory 10% withholding, declaring dividends out of untested exempt retained earnings, or structuring a bank remittance as a loan or service fee solely to avoid dividend tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI reclassification of the distribution as a dividend, assessment of the 10% withholding on the gross payment, late-payment interest, surcharges, and penalties for failure to file the corresponding withholding return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who authorizes the repatriation without required withholding is personally liable for the tax deemed collected by law and may face criminal prosecution for misappropriation of public revenues; the corporate bank account may be frozen during proceedings.
